title: T1608.004 — Stage Capabilities - Drive-by Target
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Stage Capabilities - Drive-by Target with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated diagram: an attacker stages a drive-by target on a compromised trusted news website, a hidden script sends a visiting employee's browser through redirects to an exploit server, a payload is dropped, and the SOC watches WAF, file-integrity, proxy and EDR telemetry.

nodes.label: Attacker
nodes.tip: The threat actor. Staging the drive-by target happens before any victim is involved.

nodes.label: News site
nodes.tip: A popular local news website the attacker has broken into. Victims arrive on their own - no lure is ever sent.

nodes.label: Exploit-kit gate
nodes.tip: A small attacker server behind the injected script. It checks each visitor and only attacks the chosen ones.

nodes.label: Employee browser
nodes.tip: An employee browsing the news site at work. Simply opening the page is enough to start the attack.

nodes.label: SOC analyst
nodes.tip: The defender. Joins estate telemetry, proxy redirect chains, and EDR browser events to unmask the stage.

steps.title: Scan for soft targets
steps.caption: The attacker scans many websites and looks for content-management systems that are months behind on updates. A popular local news site shows an old, unpatched version.
steps.defender: Scanning noise is visible to the targets' WAFs as fingerprint probes, but almost nobody can tell yet which site will be chosen.

detection.label: No detection
detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Compromise the trusted site
steps.caption: Using credentials stolen from a plugin developer, the attacker logs into the news site's admin panel. The site still looks perfectly normal to every visitor.
steps.defender: The CMS audit log records an admin login from an unusual country - the first strong signal, if anyone is watching.

steps.title: Inject the hidden loader
steps.caption: The attacker edits the site footer template and adds one obfuscated script tag. The script quietly loads a hidden second page that visitors never see.
steps.defender: File-integrity monitoring on the web root flags the template change within minutes.

steps.title: Arm the gate
steps.caption: On the hidden landing server the attacker configures gate checks: visitor country, browser and plugin versions, and one visit per victim. Only chosen users are attacked; everyone else sees nothing.
steps.defender: None of this is visible to ordinary visitors. Only a crawler that knows exactly where to look ever meets the gate.

steps.title: Silent redirect chain
steps.caption: An employee opens the morning news as usual. The injected script silently chains the browser through redirects to the exploit landing page. No click, no download, no warning.
steps.defender: The proxy records the redirect chain: the referer is your trusted site, the next hops are a shortener and a domain registered last week.

steps.title: Exploit runs in the browser
steps.caption: The landing code tests the browser, finds a weakness, and runs inside the browser process. The news page on screen still looks completely normal.
steps.defender: EDR sees the browser crash once, or open a local port it never uses - small signs that are easy to miss.

detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: Payload dropped and started
steps.caption: The running code fetches a small payload and starts it. On this machine the EDR blocks the launch - but on two other visitor machines outside your company it starts quietly.
steps.defender: EDR logs the browser spawning a script interpreter - a browser has no honest reason to do that.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: SOC response
steps.caption: The analyst isolates the workstation, patches the browser fleet, helps clean the news site with its hosting provider, and reports the kit infrastructure. The site owner posts a notice to its readers.
steps.defender: Hunting finds two more visitors were attacked before the block. Their hosts are cleaned too, and the injected script path is added to every watchlist.
